Empirical Research Plan:  ACA Medicaid Expansion, Near-Elderly Low-Income Adults, and Mortality  
  
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  
  
1. Identification Strategy  
   • Method:  Staggered-adoption difference-in-differences (DID) with an event-study extension.  
   • Why appropriate:  (i) Treatment—Medicaid eligibility—was switched on at clearly defined dates that differ across states but is unchanged within states before adoption; (ii) we observe several pre- and post-years; (iii) individuals are linked to their state of residence, so we can compare mortality changes in expansion states relative to never/late adopters.  
   • Estimator:  Use recent staggered-DID estimators that are robust to heterogeneous treatment effects (Callaway-Sant’Anna, Sun & Abraham, or Two-Stage-Interaction estimator available in fixest).  
  
2. Treatment and Control  
   • Treatment variable  
     T_isct = 1 if individual i in state s is observed in calendar year t that is ≥ the state’s expansion effective date (2014-01-01 for most; 2014-04-01 for MI; etc.). Once treated, always treated.  
   • Control group  
     Same eligible population (citizens, 55-64, ≤138 % FPL or <HS, non-SSI) in state-years where expansion has not yet taken place. This includes (a) always-non-expansion states, and (b) not-yet-treated observations in late expanders.  
   • Timing / event date  
     Event time g = t – E_s, where E_s is expansion year of state s. Leads g < 0 capture pre-trends; lags g ≥ 0 capture dynamic treatment effects.  
   • (No running variable; not an RDD.)  
  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
   A1. Parallel trends:  In the absence of Medicaid expansion, mortality among low-income near-elderly would have trended similarly across adopter and non-adopter states. Plausibility:  Mortality changes slowly and ACA contained no other provisions sharply differing across expansion status in 2014 for this age-income cell, so A1 is credible but must be tested.  
   A2. No anticipatory effects:  Pre-2014 mortality should not change because of expected future expansion. Reasonable—the Court decision (06/2012) limited states’ ability to expand early and near-elderly mortality is hard to manipulate in the short run.  
   A3. Stable composition (SUTVA):  Expansion in state s affects only residents of s; individuals do not immediately migrate in response (especially 55-64 year-olds). Supported by low cross-state migration in this age group.  
   A4. No concurrent, differentially timed shocks correlated with expansion and mortality (e.g., state opioid programs). Addressable with state-specific linear trends and controls.  
   A5. Accurate linkage and measurement error not different by treatment. CMS and NDI linkages are national; no reason they worsen after expansion in treated states.  
  
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  
   1. Differential pre-trends in health.  
      ▹ Test:  Event-study leads; placebo reforms (e.g., pretend expansion in 2011).  
      ▹ Mitigate:  Add state-specific linear (or quadratic) trends; control for time-varying economic covariates (unemployment, minimum wage, opioid death rate).  
   2. Spillovers to control states via hospital presumptive eligibility or cross-state care.  
      ▹ Sensitivity:  Drop border counties most likely to cross state lines.  
      ▹ Placebo:  Examine residents 65-74 (already Medicare-eligible) who should not be affected.  
   3. Treatment effect heterogeneity biasing two-way FE.  
      ▹ Use event-study estimators that explicitly aggregate cohort-specific effects (Sun-Abraham or Callaway-Sant’Anna) rather than naïve TWFE.  
  
5. R Code Outline (executable)  

```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(data.table)       # fast data handling
library(fixest)           # Sun-Abraham event study & FE
library(did)              # Callaway-Sant'Anna estimator
library(ggplot2)

# ---- 1. Load Data (assume CSVs) ----
acs      <- fread("acs_2008_2013_linked.csv")      # ACS + PIK
death    <- fread("numident_2008_2017.csv")        # death dates
cause    <- fread("mdiacs_cause_2008_2015.csv")    # NDI cause
medicaid <- fread("cms_enrollment_2008_2016.csv")  # enrollment panel
state_dates <- fread("medicaid_expansion_dates.csv") # one row per state

# ---- 2. Merge and Construct Panel ----
# Merge all sources on PIK
panel <- merge(acs, death, by = "pik", all.x = TRUE)
panel <- merge(panel, cause, by = "pik", all.x = TRUE)

# Create person-year rows 2008–2017
panel <- panel[, .(year = 2008:2017), by = pik]
panel <- merge(panel, acs, by="pik", all.x=TRUE)  # bring demographics again

# Mortality outcome
panel[, died := (death_year == year)]             # 1 if death occurs in year
panel[is.na(died), died := 0]

# Disease vs external causes (only if death==1 and cause available)
panel[, death_disease  := died * (cause_cat == "disease")]
panel[, death_external := died * (cause_cat == "external")]

# Treatment timing
panel <- merge(panel, state_dates, by = "state")  # expansion_date
panel[, treat := as.integer(year >= expansion_year)]

# Event-time indicators for Sun & Abraham
panel[, g := expansion_year]                     # cohort
panel[, event := year - g]                       # leads/lags

# Sample restrictions
panel <- panel[year >= 2008 & year <= 2017 &
               age >= 55 & age <= 64 &
               cit_us == 1 &
               inc_fpl <= 1.38 & educ < "HS" &
               ssi==0]

# ---- 3. Main Specification: Event Study ----
est <- feols(died ~ sunab(g, year) | state + year,
             data = panel, weight = ~person_weight, cluster = ~state)

# Summarize
summary(est)

# Plot dynamic effects
iplot(est) + theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Event Study: ACA Medicaid Expansion and Annual Mortality",
       x = "Years Relative to Expansion", y = "pp effect on mortality")

# ---- 4. Robustness: Callaway–Sant’Anna ----- 
cs <- att_gt(yname = "died",
             tname = "year",
             idname = "pik",
             gname = "g",
             panel = TRUE,
             xformla = ~ age + sex + race + educ + married,
             data = panel)
agg_effect <- aggte(cs, type = "dynamic")
summary(agg_effect)

# ---- 5. Additional Robustness: Drop border counties ----
panel_nb <- panel[border_to_expand_state == 0]
est_nb <- feols(died ~ sunab(g, year) | state + year,
                data = panel_nb, weight = ~person_weight, cluster = ~state)
summary(est_nb)
```

6. Expected Results  
Direction:  Medicaid expansion should lower near-elderly mortality by improving access to preventive and chronic-disease care and by reducing financial barriers to prescription drugs.  
Magnitude (back-of-envelope):  Baseline annual mortality for 55-64 low-income ≈ 1.0 % (10 per 1,000). A 5-10 % reduction (= 0.05-0.10 pp) is plausible within 3 years, larger (≈ 0.15 pp) for disease-related deaths; minimal change for external causes.  
  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
C1: Parallel pre-trends tested and hold?  → 0.8  
C2: No simultaneous confounders?          → 0.7  
C3: Stable composition / no migration?    → 0.9  
C4: Treatment correctly assigned?         → 1.0  
C5: Appropriate estimator for staggered adoption? → 0.9  
Average ≈ 0.86 → Method judged credible, but relies on verified pre-trends and careful robustness.
